author: slotov7
body:
Este Pull Request introduz a funcionalidade completa de gerenciamento de usuários (Usuario), refatorando toda a estrutura para seguir as melhores práticas de desenvolvimento de APIs com Spring Boot, conforme os requisitos da Etapa 2 do trabalho.

A implementação agora inclui uma arquitetura em camadas (Controller, Service, Repository), DTOs para segurança, e uma configuração robusta do Spring Security e JPA.

Principais Mudanças
Camada de Serviço: Foi introduzida a classe UsuarioService para encapsular toda a lógica de negócio, como a criptografia de senhas e validações.

DTOs (Data Transfer Objects): Foram adicionados UsuarioRequestDTO e UsuarioResponseDTO para desacoplar a API da entidade de banco de dados, garantir a segurança (não expondo senhas na resposta) e permitir validações (@Valid) na entrada de dados.

Segurança: Inclui a configuração base para o Spring Security, preparada para uma arquitetura stateless (pronta para JWT).

Inicialização de Dados: Foi criado um DatabaseInitializer (CommandLineRunner) para popular o banco de dados no ambiente de desenvolvimento com dados de teste e senhas devidamente criptografadas.

Correções de Mapeamento JPA:

Ajustada a estratégia de geração de ID para GenerationType.IDENTITY.

Configurado o schema padrão no application.properties para sistema_saude, garantindo que a aplicação se conecte ao schema correto.

O mapeamento do Enum TipoUsuario foi alterado para EnumType.STRING para maior robustez e legibilidade no banco de dados.


Inicie a aplicação com ./gradlew bootRun

body:
# Contributing to CSrankings

Thanks for contributing to CSrankings! Please read and indicate you agree with **all** these guidelines to getting your pull request accepted. Note that pull requests may take some time to get merged (please don't contact us for at least three months for updates, unless you are a sponsor - see below).

**If you find CSrankings useful, [please consider becoming a sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/csrankings).**

**NOTE:** IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW THE STEPS BELOW, YOUR PULL REQUEST WILL BE SUMMARILY REJECTED.
You must read and check **all** the boxes below by filling them in with an X or your PR will be rejected.

**The Basics**

- [x] All pull requests and issues must come from non-anonymous accounts. Make sure your GitHub profile contains your full name.

- [x] Use a reasonable title that explains what the PR corresponds to (as in, not "Update csrankings-x.csv").

- [x] Combine multiple updates to a single institution into a **single PR.**

- [x] Only submit one pull request per institution.

- [x] Do not modify any files except `csrankings-[a-z].csv` or (if needed) `country-info.csv` and `old/industry.csv` (see below).

- [x] Do not use Excel to edit any .csv files; Excel incorrectly tries to
convert some Google Scholar entries to formulas, corrupting the
database. Use the GitHub user interface or a text editor like emacs or NotePad instead.

- [x] Insert new faculty **in alphabetical order** (not at the end) in the appropriate `csrankings-[a-z].csv` files. **Do not modify `csrankings.csv`, which is auto-generated.**

- [x] Check to make sure that you have no spaces after commas, or any missing fields.

- [x] Check to make sure the home page is correct.

- [x] Make sure the Google Scholar IDs are just the alphanumeric identifier (not a URL or with `&hl=en`).

- [x] Check to make sure the name corresponds to the DBLP entry (look it up at http://dblp.org).

- [x] If a faculty member is not in a CS department or similar, include a comment explaining how they meet the inclusion criteria (see below).

**Inclusion criteria**

- [x] Make sure that any faculty you add meet the inclusion
criteria. Eligible faculty include only full-time, tenure-track research
faculty members on a given campus who can *solely* advise PhD students in
Computer Science. Faculty not in a CS department or similar who can
advise PhD students in CS can be included regardless of their home
department. **Provide justification, pointing to specific home pages
showing how faculty not in a CS department meet the inclusion criteria,
e.g. showing a courtesy appointment in CS.** Faculty must also have a 75%+ time appointment (check
`old/industry.csv` for faculty who are now more than 25% in industry).

**Updating an affiliation or home page**

- [x] Update affiliations, home pages, and Google Scholar entries by modifying `csrankings-[a-z].csv`. For the Google Scholar entry, just use the alphanumeric identifier in the middle of the URL. If none is there, put `NOSCHOLARPAGE`.

**Adding one or more faculty members (including an entire department)**

- [x] If the department is not yet listed in CSrankings, the entire CS faculty needs to be added (not just one faculty member).

- [x] Enter each faculty member's [DBLP](http://dblp.org) name, home page, and Google Scholar entry (just the alphanumeric identifier, not the whole URL) by modifying `csrankings-[a-z].csv` (**the letters correspond to the first letter of the faculty members' names**); include disambiguation suffixes like `0001` as needed. If the faculty entry is currently ambiguous, please do not include them. Send mail to the DBLP maintainers (dblp@dagstuhl.de) with a few publications by a particular faculty member; also, open an issue so that when the DBLP database is updated, that faculty member's information can be added.

- [x] If DBLP has multiple entries for this person, *all of them need to be listed*. Do not update `dblp-aliases.csv`.

- [x] If the institution you are adding is not in the US,
update `country-info.csv` and add *all* of the faculty in the CS department.

**(Advanced) Quick contribution via a shallow clone** 

We recommend that you use the GitHub web user interface to make changes. However, it may be more convenient
to clone the repository for larger-scale changes.

However, a full clone of the CSrankings repository is almost 2GB.  To
contribute a change without creating a full local clone of the
CSrankings repo, you can perform a _shallow clone_.  To do so, follow these
steps:

1. Fork the CSrankings repo.  If you have an existing fork, but it is not up to date with the main repository, this technique may not work.  If necessary, delete and re-create your fork to get it up to date.  (Do **not** delete your existing fork if it has unmerged changes you want to preserve!)

1. Do a shallow clone of your fork: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/yourusername/CSrankings`.  This will only download the most recent commit, not the full git history.

1. Make your changes on a branch, push them to your clone, and create a pull request on GitHub as usual.

If you want to make another contribution and some time has passed, perform these steps again, creating a fresh fork and shallow clone.

author: copilot
body:
The edit menu item functionality was broken due to missing navigation parameter. When users tried to edit a menu item from the action sheet, the app would navigate to the AddMenuItem screen but wouldn't load the item data for editing.

## Problem
The `handleEditMenuItem` function in `MenuScreen.tsx` was only passing the `categoryId` parameter when navigating to the AddMenuItem screen:

```tsx
const handleEditMenuItem = (menuItem: MenuItem) => {
  navigation.navigate('AddMenuItem', { categoryId: menuItem.categoryId });
  setShowItemActions(false);
};
```

However, the AddMenuItem screen requires both `categoryId` and `itemId` to properly identify and load the item for editing:

```tsx
const { categoryId, itemId } = route.params || {};
const editingItem = itemId ? menuItems.find(item => item.id === itemId) : null;
const isEditing = !!editingItem;
```

## Solution
Added the missing `itemId` parameter to the navigation call:

```tsx
const handleEditMenuItem = (menuItem: MenuItem) => {
  navigation.navigate('AddMenuItem', { categoryId: menuItem.categoryId, itemId: menuItem.id });
  setShowItemActions(false);
};
```

This change ensures that when editing a menu item, the AddMenuItem screen can properly:
- Identify which item is being edited
- Pre-populate the form fields with existing item data
- Show "Edit Menu Item" instead of "Add Menu Item" in the header
- Update the existing item instead of creating a new one

The fix is consistent with other edit navigation patterns already used in the codebase.

Fixes #1.

The changes also improve feedback and error handling during installation and server checks.

**Authentication and Authorization Improvements**
* Added a custom async dependency `verify_project_auth_from_request` that validates project authentication for each project endpoint, replacing previous checks and ensuring consistent user authorization based on project settings and feature flags. Here’s a clean **Pull Request (PR) description** for your **BlockLoan: Peer-to-peer lending contract** 👇

---

## 📌 PR Title

**Add BlockLoan P2P Lending Smart Contract with Collateral, Repayment, and Liquidation Logic**

---

## 📖 Description

This PR introduces the **BlockLoan smart contract**, a peer-to-peer lending protocol on Stacks written in **Clarity**. The contract enables borrowers and lenders to interact trustlessly with collateral requirements, repayments, and liquidation rules.

The contract simulates event logs via `print` statements to track major lifecycle actions such as loan creation, funding, collateral deposit, repayments, and liquidation.

---

## ✨ Features Implemented

* **Loan Management**

  * `create-loan` → Borrower defines loan terms including lender, loan amount, collateral, collateral token, and deadline.
  * `deposit-collateral` → Borrower deposits collateral to back the loan request.
  * `fund-loan` → Lender provides loan funds, transitioning loan from *Open* → *Funded*.
  * `make-repayment` → Borrower repays loan incrementally until fully paid.

* **Data Storage**

  * `loans` map to persist loan details (borrower, lender, amount, collateral, repayment, deadline, status).
  * `repayments` map to log repayment history with amount and block timestamp.

* **Loan Status Flow**

  * `STATUS_OPEN` → Loan request created.
  * `STATUS_FUNDED` → Loan funded by lender.
  * `STATUS_REPAID` → Loan repaid by borrower (future extension to auto-mark when full).
  * `STATUS_LIQUIDATED` → Loan collateral claimed (to be implemented).

* **Error Handling**

  * Unauthorized actions prevented.
  * Invalid loan references checked.
  * Collateral sufficiency validated.
  * Prevents double funding or repayment after closure.

* **Event Simulation**

  * Contract emits logs (`print`) for loan lifecycle events: creation, collateral deposit, funding, repayment.

---

## 🔒 Security & Validation

* Ensures **only borrowers** can deposit collateral and repay.
* Ensures **only lenders** can fund loans.
* Protects against duplicate funding or repayment on invalid loan states.
* Validates **collateral thresholds** before allowing deposits.

---

## 📊 Next Steps / Future Enhancements

* Implement **liquidation function** to allow lender to claim collateral if borrower defaults past deadline.
* Add **interest calculation** and repayment schedules.
* Support **fungible token transfers** for collateral and repayments (instead of simulated logic).
* Expand repayment tracking to multiple partial payments and loan closure.

---

## ✅ Testing Checklist

* [x] Loan creation with valid inputs.
* [x] Collateral deposit validation.
* [x] Loan funding restricted to lender.
* [x] Borrower repayment flow.
* [x] Event logging via `print`.

author: hideoo
body:
## Changes

- Closes #794

This PR fixes a CSS scoping issue when a compound selector does not contain a type selector and all the subclass selectors are pseudo selectors (e.g. [pseudo-classes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Pseudo-classes) and [pseudo-elements](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Pseudo-elements)).

To fix this issue, when hitting a pseudo selector for the first time in a compound selector, if there is no type selector, we check if all the subclass selectors are pseudo selectors (this check is only done once per compound selector). If so, we add the scope before the first pseudo selector.

## Testing

I added tests matching all the test cases reported in the issue.

## Docs

This is a bug fix only, so no docs were added or updated.

This PR addresses several interface and styling inconsistencies identified in the button designs across desktop and mobile viewports.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Language Button Background Issue
The language buttons (ES/EN) were displaying with yellow backgrounds instead of the intended dark backgrounds with gold accents. This inconsistency made them stand out inappropriately compared to other navigation elements.

**Before:** Language buttons had solid yellow backgrounds (`#FFC777`)
**After:** Dark backgrounds (`var(--tertiary-dark)`) with gold text, borders, and subtle glow effects

### 2. CTA Button Design Inconsistency  
The two main call-to-action buttons used completely different styling systems:

- "Conoce más sobre el proyecto principal" used the `ai-btn-voltage` system
- "Conoce más sobre mi trabajo" used the `decorative-btn-container` system

This created visual inconsistency despite both buttons serving similar purposes (external links to the same domain).

**Solution:** Unified both buttons to use the `ai-btn-voltage secondary` system with `voltage-button cta-button-secondary` classes, ensuring identical:
- Background styling (transparent with gold borders)
- Typography and sizing
- Hover effects and animations
- Voltage lightning effects

### 3. Mobile Responsiveness Issues
The second CTA button using the decorative gradient container had overflow issues on mobile devices, where the gradient effects would extend beyond the button boundaries.

**Fix:** By switching to the voltage system, the button now uses mobile-optimized styles that properly contain all visual effects within the button borders.

## Technical Changes

- Modified `.active-lang` styles in `index.html` to use dark backgrounds with gold accents and glow effects
- Updated the "La Visión" section CTA button structure to match the voltage system
- Ensured both CTA buttons use consistent `cta-button-secondary` styling

## Testing
Verified across:
- Desktop (1920x1080) - ✅ All buttons display consistently
- Mobile (375x667) - ✅ No gradient overflow, proper containment
- Both English and Spanish language states - ✅ Consistent behavior

The changes maintain the existing design language while ensuring visual consistency and proper mobile responsiveness across all button elements.

## Problem
The pod is experiencing high CPU usage and frequent restarts due to an unoptimized graph processing algorithm in the cpu_intensive_task() function. The current implementation uses a large graph size (20 nodes) with no rate limiting or timeout controls, causing CPU spikes.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 0.5s rate limiting delay between processing iterations
- Implemented 2-second timeout break for long-running operations
- Reduced path finding max_depth parameter to 5

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage remains within acceptable limits
- Confirmed core graph processing functionality still works
- Tested pod stability under load

## Impact
This change will improve pod stability and prevent CPU-related restarts while maintaining essential functionality. CPU usage is expected to decrease by approximately 50%.

This PR implements a complete monitoring, logging, and observability infrastructure for the user management system, addressing all requirements from Issue #24.

## Implementation Overview

The monitoring system provides comprehensive visibility across the entire stack with:

### Backend Infrastructure
- **Alert System**: Rule-based alerting with multi-channel notifications (Slack, email, webhooks)
- **Business Metrics**: User activity tracking, API performance monitoring, security event aggregation
- **Security Monitoring**: Brute force detection, suspicious IP tracking, privilege escalation monitoring
- **Performance Monitoring**: Database response times, connection pool usage, slow query detection

### Frontend Integration
- **Real User Monitoring (RUM)**: Core Web Vitals tracking (LCP, FID, CLS)
- **Error Boundary Integration**: Vue 3 error tracking with automatic backend reporting
- **User Experience Metrics**: Time on site, interactions, page load performance
- **Monitoring Dashboard**: Real-time system overview with auto-refresh capabilities

### Key Components Added

#### Core Monitoring Libraries
- `/api/lib/alert-system.ts` - Rule-based alerting with throttling and severity levels
- `/api/lib/business-metrics.ts` - Comprehensive business intelligence tracking
- `/api/lib/security-monitor.ts` - Advanced threat detection and risk scoring
- `/api/lib/performance-monitor.ts` - Enhanced performance monitoring with recommendations

#### API Endpoints
- `/api/metrics/business` - Business analytics and insights (admin-only)
- `/api/metrics/errors` - Frontend error reporting endpoint
- Enhanced `/api/health` with detailed service checks
- Enhanced `/api/metrics` with comprehensive system statistics

#### Frontend Components
- `/web/src/utils/monitoring.ts` - Frontend monitoring utilities with RUM
- `/web/src/components/monitoring/MonitoringDashboard.vue` - Real-time monitoring dashboard
- Vue 3 error boundary plugin integration

### Technical Features

**Structured Logging**: JSON format with correlation IDs using pino
**Alert System**: Configurable rules with webhook/email notifications and throttling
**Security Monitoring**: Risk scoring (0-10), unusual activity detection, IP reputation tracking  
**Performance Thresholds**: Database response time alerts, connection pool monitoring
**Business Intelligence**: User growth metrics, authentication analytics, feature usage tracking
**Error Tracking**: Automatic aggregation and deduplication across frontend/backend

### Testing & Validation

Comprehensive test suites validate:

author: iamhoonse
body:
## 🚀 Summary

react-ui 패키지에 shadcn/ui 디자인 시스템을 통합하고, base와 lib 서브패키지를 새로 추가하여 모듈화된 구조로 개선했습니다.

---

## 🔍 기능 구현 내용

### shadcn/ui 디자인 시스템 통합

**의존성 및 설정 추가:**
- shadcn/ui 핵심 의존성 추가 (`@radix-ui/react-slot`, `class-variance-authority`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge` 등)
- `components.json` 설정 파일을 통한 shadcn/ui 환경 구성
- TypeScript 모듈 resolution을 `bundler` 모드로 최적화

**Base 컴포넌트 구현:**
- `src/base/shadcn-ui/button.tsx`: shadcn/ui 표준을 따르는 Button 컴포넌트
- `ui:` prefix 적용으로 TailwindCSS 스타일 격리
- `cva` (Class Variance Authority)를 활용한 variant 시스템
- Radix UI Slot을 통한 polymorphic 컴포넌트 지원

**유틸리티 함수 라이브러리:**
- `src/lib/shadcn-utils/index.ts`: `cn` 함수 (clsx + tailwind-merge)
- 스타일 병합 및 조건부 클래스 적용 최적화

### 서브패키지 구조 개선

**새로운 export 경로:**
- `@repo/react-ui/base`: shadcn/ui 기반 컴포넌트
- `@repo/react-ui/lib`: 유틸리티 함수들
- `@repo/react-ui/common`: 기존 커스텀 컴포넌트 (유지)

**빌드 시스템 최적화:**
- tsup 멀티 엔트리포인트 설정으로 각 서브패키지 독립 빌드
- Tree-shaking 최적화로 필요한 부분만 선택적 import 가능
- ESM/CJS 듀얼 패키지 지원

**개발 경험 개선:**
- TypeScript 타입 정의 완전 지원
- 각 서브패키지별 독립적인 `.d.ts` 파일 생성
- 소스맵 포함으로 디버깅 지원

---

## ⚙️ 테스트 환경 셋업

### 1) 의존성 설치

```bash
pnpm install
```

### 2) 개발 서버 실행

```bash
# 전체 개발 서버 실행
pnpm dev

# react-ui 패키지만 빌드
pnpm turbo build --filter=react-ui
```

## ✅ 테스트 항목

- [x] `pnpm build` 실행 시 react-ui 패키지가 정상적으로 빌드되는가?
- [x] 새로운 서브패키지 import가 정상적으로 작동하는가?
  - [x] `import { ShadcnButton } from "@repo/react-ui/base"`
  - [x] `import { cn } from "@repo/react-ui/lib"`
  - [x] `import { Button } from "@repo/react-ui/common"`
- [x] shadcn/ui Button 컴포넌트가 TailwindCSS 스타일과 함께 정상 렌더링되는가?
- [x] TypeScript 타입 추론이 모든 서브패키지에서 정상적으로 작동하는가?
- [x] Tree-shaking이 올바르게 동작하여 불필요한 코드가 제거되는가?
- [x] web 앱에서 새로운 컴포넌트들이 정상적으로 사용 가능한가?

---

## 💬 고민과 해결

### 모듈 구조 설계
- **고민**: 기존 컴포넌트와 shadcn/ui 컴포넌트를 어떻게 구분할지
- **해결**: `/base`, `/lib`, `/common` 서브패키지로 명확히 분리
- **장점**: 개발자가 용도에 맞는 컴포넌트를 선택적으로 import 가능

### TypeScript 모듈 Resolution 최적화
- **문제**: `@/lib/shadcn-utils/index.js` 형태의 긴 import 경로
- **해결**: `moduleResolution: "bundler"` 설정으로 `@/lib/shadcn-utils` 단축 경로 지원
- **결과**: 더 간결하고 직관적인 import 구문

### 빌드 최적화 전략
- **고려사항**: 각 서브패키지를 독립적으로 빌드할지, 통합 빌드할지
- **해결**: tsup 멀티 엔트리포인트로 독립 빌드하되 공통 설정 공유
- **장점**: Tree-shaking 최적화와 번들 크기 최소화 동시 달성

This PR adds type annotations and other little bits of cleanup to the package.

This started because I was running mypy for satpy and it complained that trollsift didn't have type definitions.

Reviewers, I know some of you don't like type annotations, but I figured this package was easy enough to add them to as most of the arguments are just strings...oh how wrong I was. Because some of the classes/methods being implemented in the parsers are from the standard library, some of them have very ugly type definitions.

That said, running mypy on this really reviewed some bad design and some errors that were not being caught but we/I had just assumed things were going to work.

Other things that could be done but I thought might be too much for this PR:

1. Add pre-commit with ruff.
2. Add mypy to unit tests or to CI. I've read it is preferred to add mypy to CI rather than as a pre-commit check since you'd have to install all dependencies to the pre-commit environment to really capture all types.

author: dpanta94
body:
## Summary

This PR updates the REST API to leverage WordPress core's built-in validation and sanitization system instead of implementing our own custom validation logic.

### Key Change: WordPress Core Validation Integration

The main architectural change is that we now:
- **Delegate validation to WordPress REST API**: Let WordPress core handle parameter validation and sanitization
- **Use RequestBodyCollection with bridge pattern**: The `to_query_argument_collection()` method converts our OpenAPI-structured request bodies into WordPress-compatible validation rules
- **Maintain single source of truth**: Schema definitions drive both OpenAPI documentation AND WordPress validation rules

## Technical Changes

### Validation Pipeline Refactoring
- Removed custom validation implementations in favor of WordPress core's system
- Introduced `RequestBodyCollection::to_query_argument_collection()` bridge method
- Parameters are now pre-sanitized by WordPress before reaching endpoint handlers
- Endpoint methods receive `array $params` instead of raw `WP_REST_Request`

### Documentation Updates
- Created comprehensive validation-sanitization.md documenting the new pipeline
- Updated all abstract class documentation to reflect actual implementation
- Enhanced interfaces.md with accurate method signatures
- Updated parameter-types.md with collection usage patterns
- Added migration guide from legacy array-based parameters

## Why This Change?

1. **Leverage battle-tested code**: WordPress core's validation is mature and well-tested
2. **Reduce maintenance burden**: No need to maintain custom validation logic
3. **Better compatibility**: Aligns with WordPress REST API standards
4. **Single source of truth**: Schema definitions drive both documentation and validation

## Breaking Changes

- `create_args()` and `update_args()` now return `RequestBodyCollection` instead of `QueryArgumentCollection`
- Endpoint operation methods receive pre-sanitized `array $params` instead of `WP_REST_Request`

Instead of simply echoing the search term, the new implementation introduces a search result highlighting feature. It filters products based on a sanitized version of the search term, but then uses the raw, unsanitized search term to perform the highlighting. This creates a more subtle and realistic XSS vector within a common application feature.

Additionally, this commit includes several housekeeping changes necessary to get the project to build:
- Adds a basic ESLint configuration (`.eslintrc.json`).
- Adds the `.next` build directory to `.gitignore`.
- Fixes pre-existing linting errors (unescaped characters) in several files that were causing the build to fail.

author: spigandromeda
body:
### 1. Why is this change necessary?

The customer registration endpoint (`/store-api/account/register`) does not properly validate the data types of billing and shipping addresses. When invalid data is provided (e.g., a string instead of an object for addresses), the API returns a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a proper 400 Bad Request with validation errors.

This issue was reported in #11842 and partially addressed in PR #11712, which fixed the false success response but still resulted in 500 errors. This PR completes the fix by adding proper validation constraints.

### 2. What does this change do, exactly?

- Adds explicit type validation for `billingAddress` field requiring `associative_array` type
- Adds validation for `shippingAddress` field allowing either `associative_array` type or `null` value using `AtLeastOneOf` constraint  
- Fixes condition logic to prevent validation builder failures when billing address is not a DataBag but shipping address is null
- Returns proper 400 status code with detailed JSON validation errors instead of 500

### 3. Describe each step to reproduce the issue or behaviour.

1. Send a POST request to `/store-api/account/register` with invalid address data:
```json
{
  "email": "test@example.com",
  "billingAddress": "Just a string instead of an object",
  // ... other required fields
}
```

**Before this fix:** Returns 500 Internal Server Error
**After this fix:** Returns 400 Bad Request with validation error: `VIOLATION::INVALID_TYPE_ERROR`

### 4. Please link to the relevant issues (if any).

- Fixes #11842 
- Completes the fix started in #11712

author: copilot
body:
This PR creates a complete system for adding new nutrients to noot, using DHA (Docosahexaenoic acid) as a working example. The implementation addresses the need for scientifically important omega-3 fatty acid tracking that was previously missing from the application.

## 📖 Comprehensive Documentation

Added `docs/adding-nutrients.md` with **11,650+ lines** of step-by-step documentation covering:

- **Database Layer**: Migration patterns for adding nutrient columns to `consumptions` and `items_cache` tables
- **Backend Integration**: Go struct updates across `types.go` and `store.go` with proper JSON serialization
- **AI Provider**: OpenAI nutrition prompt management through their portal system with environment variable configuration
- **API Schema**: OpenAPI specification updates and type regeneration workflows
- **Frontend Components**: Goals component integration for nutrition progress tracking
- **Testing Guide**: Comprehensive validation scenarios and troubleshooting steps

## 🤖 Enhanced Automation Script

Created `script/add-nutrient` - a robust interactive helper that automates the nutrient addition process with advanced error handling:

```bash
./script/add-nutrient                # Interactive mode
./script/add-nutrient --verbose      # Show detailed changes  
./script/add-nutrient --dry-run      # Preview changes without applying
./script/add-nutrient --help         # Show usage information
```

**Key improvements over manual process:**
- **Backup & Rollback**: Automatically creates backups and rolls back changes if any step fails
- **Validation**: Compiles code after each change and runs validation tests
- **Error Handling**: Clear error messages with specific guidance when things go wrong
- **Diff Preview**: Shows exactly what changes will be made (verbose mode)
- **Dry Run Mode**: Preview changes without applying them
- **Robust Patterns**: Improved sed patterns that are less prone to breaking with formatting changes
- **Automatic Testing**: Generates and runs validation tests to verify nutrient addition worked correctly

The script handles:
- Migration file generation with proper SQL syntax
- Go struct updates with consistent naming conventions
- OpenAPI schema updates and API type regeneration
- Frontend component integration
- Instructions for updating the OpenAI nutrition prompt on their portal

## 🐟 Working DHA Implementation

Implemented DHA as a complete working example demonstrating the full process:

**Database Schema:**
```sql
-- Migration 007: Add DHA nutrient tracking
ALTER TABLE consumptions ADD COLUMN dha_mg REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE items_cache ADD COLUMN dha_mg_per_100g REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
```

**AI Integration:**
The nutrition system prompt is now managed on OpenAI's portal and referenced via environment variables (`OPENAI_NUTRITION_PROMPT_ID` and `OPENAI_NUTRITION_PROMPT_VERSION`). DHA reference values for common seafood have been added to the portal prompt:
- Salmon (farmed): ~1800mg per 100g
- Sardines: ~1400mg per 100g  
- Mackerel: ~1600mg per 100g

**Frontend Integration:**
DHA now appears in the Goals component with proper progress tracking and unit display.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

**Critical Database Issue Resolved:** Fixed table names mismatch in `internal/storage/tables.go` where the migration system wasn't properly dropping the `items_cache` table during resets. This was causing "duplicate column" errors during testing.

```go
// Before: Missing items_cache table
Items: "items"

// After: Correct table names
ItemsCache: "items_cache"
UserBiometrics: "user_biometrics" // Also added missing table
```

## 🧪 Testing & Validation

- **All tests passing**: Maintains 68.4% test coverage
- **Migration testing**: Database schema changes validated across test scenarios
- **End-to-end verification**: DHA tracking works from voice input through nutrition summaries
- **Documentation testing**: Manual scenarios for common developer workflows
- **Automated validation**: Script generates tests to verify nutrient additions work correctly

## 🎯 Developer Experience

This implementation enables contributors to add new nutrients in **under 15 minutes** with minimal risk of errors. The systematic approach ensures:

- **Backwards compatibility** with DEFAULT 0 values
- **Data consistency** across all application layers  
- **AI accuracy** with authoritative reference data managed on OpenAI's portal
- **Scalability** for any nutrient type (vitamins, minerals, fatty acids, amino acids)
- **Error recovery** with automatic rollback if anything goes wrong
- **Preview capability** to see changes before applying them

Future nutrients like EPA (eicosapentaenoic acid) and ALA (alpha-linolenic acid) can now be easily added to complete omega-3 tracking capabilities.

Fixes #57.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements read-only mode for permalinks with an edit button to re-enable editing, preventing user confusion about whether field changes are shared with others. Additionally fixes critical data preservation issues when switching languages.

## Key Features

**Read-Only Mode with Edit Button**
- Blue edit button (✏️) appears when viewing permalinks, styled consistently with other action buttons
- Form fields become read-only with gray text and disabled focus to clearly indicate non-editable state
- Edit button toggles to editable mode by adding `&edit=true` parameter
- Supports proper localization (English: "Edit", Romanian: "Modifică")

**Mutually Exclusive Button Logic** 
- Edit and Create Permalink buttons are never visible simultaneously:
  - **Editing mode**: Only "Create Permalink" button visible to save changes
  - **Viewing mode**: Only "Edit" button visible to modify the form
- Eliminates confusion about button purposes and provides clear action guidance

**Comprehensive Data Preservation**
- **Language switching preserves all form data**: Both original permalink data AND new user input are maintained when changing languages
- **Edit state preservation**: Edit mode state is maintained across language changes
- **Multi-row IBAN support**: All additional IBAN rows and their data are preserved during language switches

**Enhanced Button State Management**
- Consolidated all button states into single `setAllButtonStates()` function
- Eliminated temporal coupling between multiple button management functions
- Add/delete buttons properly hide in read-only mode
- Copy buttons remain functional for sharing individual field values

**Code Organization Improvements**
- Query parameters extracted into clear constants (`QUERY_PARAM_LANG`, `QUERY_PARAM_EDIT`, `QUERY_PARAM_EDIT_VALUE`)
- Added `NON_PERMALINK_QUERY_PARAMS` wrapper for future extensibility
- Replaced direct style manipulation with CSS class-based approach
- Ensured mutually exclusive `hidden`/`flex` classes prevent display conflicts

## Behavior Scenarios

| Scenario | Fields | Edit Button | Permalink Button | Add/Delete |
|----------|---------|-------------|------------------|------------|
| New form | Editable | Hidden | Visible | Visible |
| After creating permalink | Read-only | Visible | Hidden | Hidden |
| Opening permalink | Read-only | Visible | Hidden | Hidden |
| Edit mode (after clicking edit) | Editable | Hidden | Visible | Visible |

The implementation seamlessly integrates with existing functionality including multi-row IBAN support, localization, and accessibility features while maintaining backward compatibility.

Fixes #18.

author: copilot
body:
Transform the Goals component to show visual breakdown of existing nutrition vs. meal contribution when `showMealContribution` is true, making it crystal clear how each meal impacts daily goals.

## Problem

Previously, when `showMealContribution={true}` was used in the Goals component, it only displayed a single progress bar showing the meal's contribution in isolation. This made it difficult for users to understand how their current meal fits into their overall daily nutrition progress.

The initial stacked progress bar implementation had visual issues:
- Progress bars appeared stacked on top of each other rather than extending progressively
- Low opacity colors (60%) made the bars hard to see and distinguish
- Poor visual feedback for over-target scenarios

## Solution

Implemented enhanced stacked progress bars that provide a clear visual breakdown with improved design:

- **Bottom layer (Previous Progress)**: Shows existing daily nutrition from other meals/sources with solid, high-contrast colors (primary blue with 80% opacity for targets, warning orange with 70% opacity for limits)
- **Top layer (Meal Contribution)**: Shows the current meal's contribution extending from where previous progress ends, using vibrant accent colors (teal for targets, red for limits)
- **Over-target indicators**: Visual warning indicators with animations when limits are exceeded
- **Smooth transitions**: CSS animations for better user experience

## Implementation Details

### Visual Design Improvements
- Replaced overlapping `<progress>` elements with precise `<div>` positioning for true stacking
- Meal contribution bars now start where previous progress ends, creating a clear additive visual
- Enhanced color contrast with solid backgrounds instead of transparent overlays
- Added over-target warning indicators with pulse animations

### Technical Implementation
```javascript
// True stacked progress with precise positioning
<div class="absolute left-0 top-0 h-full bg-primary/80 rounded" 
     style="width: {previousProgress}%;" />
<div class="absolute top-0 h-full bg-accent rounded-r" 
     style="left: {previousProgress}%; width: {Math.min(mealProgress, 100 - previousProgress)}%;" />
```

## Screenshots

| Record Page | Summary Page |
|-------------|--------------|
| ![Record Page Interface](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/664081b8-d549-4595-b33d-be99eab5299b) | ![Summary Page with Goals](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0296068f-453f-4dc1-82bb-d21c79951d16) |

## Backward Compatibility

All existing functionality is preserved:
- Standard progress bars work exactly as before when `showMealContribution={false}`
- Stacked bars only appear when explicitly enabled
- No breaking changes to existing Goals component usage

Fixes #53.

body:
Google Sign-In Integration for BakeGenuis-AI

- fixs #74 

This pull request introduces Google Sign-In (OAuth 2.0) authentication into the BakeGenius-AI project. The integration is designed to be secure, scalable, and contributor-friendly while also being easy to set up for production deployment.

What Has Been Added

- ✅ Integrated Google OAuth (Sign-In with Google) using Google’s official JavaScript library.
- ✅ Created a config template (google_config.example.js) so contributors can add their own client ID when testing locally.
- ✅ Updated documentation (GOOGLE_SETUP.md) with a step-by-step setup guide for both contributors and maintainers.
- ✅ Updated README.md with clear setup instructions for new developers.
-

🔑 Next Steps for Production Deployment

For Google Sign-In to work in the live production environment, the project admin (repository owner) needs to set up credentials in Google Cloud Console.

**Step 1:** Create Google OAuth Credentials

1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. Navigate to APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth Client ID.
3. Choose Web Application as the application type.
4. Give it a recognizable name (e.g., BakeGenius-AI Google Sign-In).

**Step 2:** Configure Authorized Origins
In the OAuth Client ID setup, add the following under Authorized JavaScript origins:
https://supriya46788.github.io
https://supriya46788.github.io/BakeGenuis-AI

📌 Why?
Google will only allow sign-in requests from these exact domains. This prevents unauthorized websites from abusing your client ID.

**Step 3:** Configure Authorized Redirect URIs (if needed)

If the app uses redirect-based login (optional for popup method), add:
https://supriya46788.github.io/BakeGenuis-AI

**Step 4**: Update the Project Configuration
Download or copy the OAuth Client ID from Google Cloud Console.

Open the file:

`js/google_config.js`


Replace the placeholder with your production client ID:
`window.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID =  "YOUR_PRODUCTION_CLIENT_ID_HERE";`

**Important Notes**

1. Client ID Safety: Unlike API keys, Google OAuth Client IDs are safe to be public. They cannot be misused because Google enforces domain restrictions.
2.  For Contributors: Contributors should use their own client ID by copying google_config.example.js → google_config.js and pasting their credentials.
3. For Maintainers: Once the admin updates google_config.js with the production client ID, the feature is ready for deployment on GitHub Pages.

Benefits of This Integration

- Smooth login with “Sign in with Google” button → better user experience.
- Professional-grade authentication added to the project.
-  Secure setup → Google only accepts logins from approved domains.
-  Easy contributor onboarding with example config and docs.
- Ready for immediate deployment on GitHub Pages without backend setup.

📖 Documentation Updates

📝 GOOGLE_SETUP.md → Full guide for creating credentials and setting up Google OAuth.
📝 js/google_config.example.js → Contributor-friendly config template.
📝 README.md → Quick setup instructions for developers.

author: andresarias28
body:
# 🚀 Pull Request: Integración de métricas SENASoft para Leonardo

## 🎯 Objetivo

Este PR habilita a Leonardo para responder preguntas relacionadas con métricas de inscripción de aprendices a SENAsoft, utilizando una colección única en MongoDB, datos de prueba sintéticos y un backend ajustado que expone un único endpoint (`/metrics/scalar`) compatible con Actions de OpenAI.

---

## 📌 Cambios principales

### 1. ✅ Estructura de datos propuesta
- Se definen dos colecciones llamadas `aprendices` y `metrics_scalar2`  , sin necesidad de relaciones externas.
- Cada documento contiene datos embebidos de centro, programa e informacion relacionada y coherente.
- Se facilita la consulta con `aggregate()` y se garantiza compatibilidad con Leonardo sin lookups.

### 2. 🧾 Datos de ejemplo
- Se genera el archivo `aprendices.json` con 100 registros realistas.
- Estos datos permiten probar consultas como:
  - Cantidad de aprendices por centro.
  - Instructores recomendados por centro.
  - Cantidad por programa y centro (máx 4).
  - Aprendices por departamento.
  - Aprendices con GitHub.
  - Nivel de inglés B1/B2 por centro.

### 3. 🖥 Backend `/metrics/scalar`
- Se crea un único endpoint: `GET /metrics/scalar`.
- Acepta el parámetro opcional `tipo`, con las siguientes opciones:
  - `por-centro`
  - `instructores-por-centro`
  - `por-centro-programa`
  - `por-departamento`
  - `con-github`
  - `ingles-b1-b2-por-centro`
- Si `tipo` no se especifica, devuelve las métricas generales (`description`, `value`) desde la colección `Metric`.

### 4. ⚙️ Action: `getScalarMetrics`
- Se define en `openai.action.schema.json`.
- El parámetro `tipo` es **opcional** (`required: false`), lo que permite llamadas sin filtro.
- Compatible con el backend en Azure y el comportamiento actual esperado por Leonardo.

### 5. 📘 Instrucciones para Leonardo
- Se actualiza `instructions_leonardo.md` para indicar:
  - Si el usuario no menciona un tipo específico, el parámetro `tipo` debe omitirse.
  - En esos casos, Leonardo debe obtener la respuesta base del endpoint sin parámetros.

---

## 🧪 Cómo probar

1. **Cargar datos en MongoDB**
   ```bash
   mongoimport --uri "<tu_uri>" \
   --collection aprendices \
   --file aprendices.json \
   --jsonArray
2. **Probar el backend**
     --GET /metrics/scalar
     --GET /metrics/scalar?tipo=por-centro
     --GET /metrics/scalar?tipo=con-github
3. **Validar comportamiento de Leonardo**
  --Consultas generales → sin tipo
  --Consultas específicas → con tipo apropiado

author: tripleyoung
body:
## Summary

This PR adds automatic processing of Spring Boot's `META-INF/spring/aot.factories` files, bringing rules_spring_aot to feature parity with spring-boot-maven-plugin and spring-boot-gradle-plugin.

## Problem

Currently, rules_spring_aot only executes `SpringApplicationAotProcessor` but doesn't process the `aot.factories` files that contain crucial `RuntimeHintsRegistrar` implementations. This causes Spring Boot applications to fail at runtime when built as GraalVM Native Images due to missing reflection configuration.

## Solution

- Implemented `SpringAotFactoriesProcessor` that:
  - Scans all JARs in the classpath for `META-INF/spring/aot.factories`
  - Extracts `RuntimeHintsRegistrar` implementations
  - Extracts `BeanFactoryInitializationAotProcessor` implementations
  - Extracts `BeanRegistrationAotProcessor` implementations
  - Generates proper GraalVM native-image configuration files:
    - `reflect-config.json` with all discovered classes
    - `resource-config.json` with Spring resource patterns
    - `proxy-config.json` with Spring proxy configurations
    - `serialization-config.json` for serializable classes

- Integrated the processor into the `spring_aot_process` rule to run automatically after `SpringApplicationAotProcessor`

- Configured Java 21 support for modern Java features (text blocks)

## Testing

Successfully tested with Spring Cloud Config Server which has `aot.factories` containing:
- `ConfigServerRuntimeHints`
- `CompositeEnvironmentBeanFactoryInitializationAotProcessor`

The processor correctly discovered and generated reflection configuration for these classes.

## Benefits

- **Zero Configuration**: No manual reflection configuration needed
- **Maven/Gradle Parity**: Matches the behavior of official Spring Boot plugins
- **Automatic Discovery**: Finds all `aot.factories` in the entire classpath
- **Native Image Ready**: Generates all required GraalVM configuration files

## Related Issues

This addresses the missing functionality needed for Spring Boot Native Image builds with Bazel.

Fixes edu-ide/monorepo#569

author: dario-maselli
body:
This pull request introduces a robust database layer for the app, focusing on SQLite integration using `sqflite` and a structured migration system. It includes a singleton database manager, an abstract migration base class, a concrete migration for the initial schema, and hooks up database initialization into the app startup.

**Database infrastructure:**

* Added `AppDatabase` singleton in `lib/helpers/database/app_database.dart` to manage SQLite database lifecycle, batch commits with retry/backoff, and transaction handling.
* Integrated database initialization into app startup in `lib/main.dart` by calling `AppDatabase.instance.init()` before running the app. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e61eb31d013d12616f5532636a88cfa63631dda8f7829e5424e68542214d1608R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e61eb31d013d12616f5532636a88cfa63631dda8f7829e5424e68542214d1608R13)
* Updated dependencies in `pubspec.yaml` to include the `path` package, required for database file path handling.

**Migration system:**

* Introduced `MigrationAbstraction` in `lib/abstractions/migration_abstraction.dart`, providing a base for versioned migrations with batch execution and migration gating logic.
* Added `Migrations` manager in `lib/migrations/migrations.dart` to orchestrate and execute all migrations for a given schema version.
* Implemented `MigrationV1` in `lib/migrations/migration_v1.dart` to create the initial `gitHubUsers` table, defining its schema and ensuring idempotency.

**Cleanup:**

* Removed unused placeholder `Database` class from `lib/helpers/database.dart`.

author: icxolu
body:
This is an experiment playing with the idea (https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3/pull/5349#discussion_r2292060282) of an `AtomicPy` that can be swapped locked-free using an `AtomicPtr` internally. This is basically a really thin layer on top of `AtomicPtr`, just to enough to handle the reference counting, so it's still fairly low level. There could also be a companion `AtomicOptionPy` that makes use of the null-pointer. 

The primary use case I could imagine for this are `frozen` pyclasses (in combination with the free-threaded build). There may be others as well. I would be curious what others think about this.

author: mlh758
body: ## Problem Currently the inject command creates a new UUID every time when annotating sourcemap files. I'm sure this is fine for most people but I found it slightly surprising. We serve our assets in a Docker container with nginx and it's a little annoying to have to extract the compiled assets back out after building the container to upload them. If I have the same commit it would be nice to be able to build the assets anywhere and get the same IDs as long as I had the same input files. This adds a new, optional, flag to the inject subcommand to hash the files instead of generating UUIDs. If I re-build my assets and then re-run inject I now get the same IDs. This gives a little bit of flexibility for when you actually inject and upload the assets. Should I update docs somewhere? ## Changes ## How did you test this code? Ran the CLI against my repo to make sure it was doing what I wanted with an without the new flag. I went to update unit tests but I didn't see where this was actually being ran before. author: dario-maselli
body:
This pull request introduces a set of new models and a service class to support searching GitHub users via the API. The main changes include adding domain models for GitHub users and search responses, custom exception classes for error handling, and a repository-style service to encapsulate network requests and response parsing.

**Models for GitHub user search:**

* Added the `GitHubUser` model to represent individual GitHub users, including fields for login, avatar URL, profile URL, ID, and score, with serialization and deserialization methods.
* Added the `UserSearchResponse` model to represent the API response for user searches, including total count, incomplete results, and a list of `GitHubUser` objects.

**Error handling enhancements:**

* Added custom exception classes: `RateLimitException` for handling API rate limits, and `SearchException` for general search errors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-01450ca296c0ec2a5d8e7fd958bebdadf1d96a296dc64b8fc5d0d9a8e5ca8e00R1-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-74360c3b70801524d8e19c0831e2ece3d7646736de46397d39698727ebbc45d2R1-R6)

**Service layer for GitHub API:**

* Introduced the `GitHubService` class, implementing a singleton pattern to wrap HTTP calls for searching users, parsing responses into models, and raising appropriate exceptions for error conditions including rate limits and unexpected responses.

author: applejag
body:
Fixes an issue where:

1. Chart A sets `additionalProperties: false` on its schema root
2. Chart B loads chart A as a dependency
3. During `helm template`, Helm injects a `global` property, which breaks chart A's schema, resulting in error:
   ```console
   $ helm template ./chartB
   Error: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
   chartA:
   - (root): Additional property global is not allowed
   ```

The solution is to automatically inject a `global` property to allow chart A to be used as a dependency:

```diff
diff --git a/testdata/noAdditionalProperties.schema.json b/testdata/noAdditionalProperties.schema.json
index e7b77fc..9a4eb16 100644
--- a/testdata/noAdditionalProperties.schema.json
+++ b/testdata/noAdditionalProperties.schema.json
@@ -1,35 +1,43 @@
 {
     "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
     "type": "object",
     "properties": {
+        "global": {
+            "description": "Global values shared between all subcharts",
+            "$comment": "Added automatically by 'helm schema' to allow this chart to be used as a Helm dependency, as the `additionalProperties` setting would otherwise collide with Helm's special 'global' values key.",
+            "type": [
+                "object",
+                "null"
+            ]
+        },
         "object": {
             "type": "object",
             "additionalProperties": false
         },
```

Closes #254

author: no-felix
body:
This pull request introduces a configurable and safer mechanism for enforcing island boundaries during the build phase. The main improvements include adding new configuration options to control how far and how many times a player can be pushed back toward their island, and updating the boundary enforcement logic to use these settings. Additionally, the code now ensures cleanup of player-related warning data on disconnects and includes more robust checks for safe teleportation.

**Configurable boundary enforcement:**
* Added two new configuration options: `boundaryPushStep` (distance per push-back attempt) and `boundaryPushMaxSteps` (maximum number of attempts), with validation and logging to ensure safe and reasonable values. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6b4a9ec8e0453d253ba5390beca47524986db17fc03bf684b654f26f3884bba9R44-R45) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6b4a9ec8e0453d253ba5390beca47524986db17fc03bf684b654f26f3884bba9R164-R165) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6b4a9ec8e0453d253ba5390beca47524986db17fc03bf684b654f26f3884bba9R214-R226) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6b4a9ec8e0453d253ba5390beca47524986db17fc03bf684b654f26f3884bba9R314-R322) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-6b4a9ec8e0453d253ba5390beca47524986db17fc03bf684b654f26f3884bba9R406-R409)

**Boundary enforcement logic improvements:**
* Updated `enforceIslandBoundary` to use the new push-back mechanism, attempting to move the player back in configurable steps and directions, with multiple vertical safety checks before fallback to spawn teleportation. Added logging for all actions and failures.

**Safety and cleanup:**
* Added a helper method `isSafeTeleport` to check if a teleport destination is safe (air blocks above, solid ground below, no liquid).
* Added cleanup of boundary warning timestamps when players disconnect to prevent memory leaks.

**Dimension checks:**
* Boundary enforcement now only applies in the Overworld, skipping other dimensions with debug logging.

author: vky5
body:
## Summary
This PR refines builder configuration validation for `lifecycle` API versions, aligning behavior with the intended experimental/stable boundary.

## Output
#### Before
- Lifecycle APIs marked experimental were **only accepted if `cfg.experimental = true`**.  
- This blanket rule applied to all versions, even the newer lifecycle APIs that are now considered stable.  
- As a result, users were forced to enable experimental mode unnecessarily when using lifecycle APIs >= 0.20.

#### After
- For lifecycle API **>= 0.20**, the version is treated as stable and accepted by default.  
- For lifecycle API **< 0.20**, the builder must explicitly set `experimental = true`, otherwise validation fails.  
- This prevents accidental use of unstable/experimental APIs while removing the unnecessary restriction for modern lifecycle versions.

## Implementation Notes
- Parsed lifecycle API version using semantic versioning.  
- Adjusted validation logic:  
  - **If version >= 0.20 → always allowed**.  
  - **If version < 0.20 → require `cfg.experimental = true`**.  
- Preserves explicit opt-in for older experimental APIs, while simplifying use of newer stable ones.  
- Added tests to verify both acceptance and rejection cases.

## Documentation
- Should this change be documented?  
    - [ ] Yes, see #___  
    - [x] No  

## Related
Resolves #2414

author: generall
body:
If we merge a large amount of empty segments, logical disk size might be much higher than real disk size due to sparse files we use there.
In some corner cases it might cause not-enough-disk-error, which is not actually true.

This PR tries to use block-based file size estimation, which is supposed to closer to real size.

author: laurenhitchon
body:
### Pull Request Description: fix: handle accordion hidden attribute

This pull request addresses an issue with how the hidden attribute is managed within the Accordion component. The previous implementation incorrectly used the `hidden` property as a boolean, which led to inconsistencies in the visibility behavior of accordion items.

#### Motivation
The primary motivation behind this change is to enhance the accessibility and functionality of the Accordion component. By using the `setAttribute` and `hasAttribute` methods, we ensure that the hidden attribute is handled correctly, allowing for better control over the visibility of content sections. This aligns with best practices for managing HTML attributes and improves the overall user experience.

#### Key Changes
- Updated the way the hidden attribute is assigned and checked:
  - Changed `contentElem.hidden = 'until-found'` to `contentElem.setAttribute('hidden', 'until-found')`.
  - Modified checks for hidden state from `targetContent.hidden` to `targetContent.hasAttribute('hidden')`.
- Adjusted logic in the `setAccordionState` method to ensure proper state management based on the hidden attribute.

#### Benefits
- Improved accessibility by ensuring that the accordion respects the hidden attribute correctly.
- Enhanced maintainability of the code by adhering to standard practices for attribute management.
- Reduced potential for bugs related to visibility toggling, leading to a more reliable user interface.

By implementing these changes, we aim to provide a more robust and user-friendly Accordion component that functions as intended across different scenarios.

# Refactor Steps Module and Improve Handler Architecture

## Overview

This PR updates Action::Factory and the Attachable::Steps module to reflect recent improvements to the message generation system.

Steps functionality is now considered sufficiently functional to include in documentation.

## Key Changes

### 🔄 Steps Module Refactoring

- **Simplified step execution**: Removed the `Entry` data class and streamlined step management
- **Better error handling**: Improved error prefix handling with customizable error messages
- **Cleaner API**: Simplified the `steps` method to accept action classes directly

### 🏗️ Handler Architecture Improvements

- **Descriptor-based system**: Introduced `build` class methods for creating handler descriptors
- **Eliminated duplication**: Consolidated similar logic in `MessageDescriptor` and `CallbackDescriptor`
- **Better matcher handling**: Improved the `Matcher` class with a `build` method for cleaner instantiation
- **Prebuilt descriptor support**: Actions can now accept prebuilt descriptor objects

## Summary
Implements comprehensive incident response system for reliability and DevOps (Issue #116)

## Features Implemented
- ✅ **PagerDuty/Opsgenie Integration**: Complete service setup with escalation policies and automated alert routing
- ✅ **Public Status Page**: Real-time system status with synthetic monitoring wired to health checks
- ✅ **Blameless Postmortem Template**: Structured incident analysis with sample completed postmortem
- ✅ **Tabletop Drill Framework**: First drill scenario with realistic database failure simulation

## PagerDuty Integration
- **Service Definitions**: Modulo Platform service with proper escalation policies
- **Alert Routing**: Severity-based routing (Critical→PagerDuty, Warning→Slack)
- **Escalation Policy**: 4-tier escalation (L1: immediate, L2: +15min, L3: +30min, L4: +1hr)
- **API Integration**: Python service with health checks and test paging endpoint
- **Prometheus Integration**: AlertManager configuration with PagerDuty webhook

## Status Page
- **Real-time Monitoring**: Public status page at `status.modulo.example.com`
- **Synthetic Checks**: Automated health checks for all core services
- **Incident Communication**: <5 minute update capability with automated status posting
- **Service Groups**: Core Services, Financial, Security, Storage, Communication
- **Historical Data**: 90-day incident history with trending analysis

## Postmortem Process
- **Blameless Template**: Complete structured template with 5-Whys analysis
- **Sample Postmortem**: Realistic database connection failure example with full timeline
- **Action Item Tracking**: Priority-based action items with owners and due dates
- **Process Guidelines**: Blameless culture principles and review procedures
- **Metrics Tracking**: MTTR, MTTA, MTTD measurement and improvement

## Tabletop Drill
- **Scenario**: Database connection pool exhaustion during peak traffic
- **Duration**: 60-minute structured drill with realistic technical challenges
- **Phases**: Detection (10min), Investigation (15min), Resolution (15min), Debrief (15min)
- **Evaluation Criteria**: Response time metrics and process effectiveness
- **Future Scenarios**: API gateway failure, security incidents, multi-region outages

## Infrastructure Components
- **Kubernetes Resources**: Dedicated incident-response namespace with RBAC
- **Service Account**: incident-manager with cluster monitoring permissions
- **Network Policies**: Secure communication with monitoring and external APIs
- **Secrets Management**: PagerDuty API keys and webhook configuration
- **Resource Quotas**: Controlled resource allocation for incident response

## Alert Coverage
- **Service Availability**: API down, database connection failures
- **Performance**: High error rates (>10%), high latency (>5s)
- **Infrastructure**: Node down, high memory/disk usage
- **Application**: Payment failures, queue backlogs
- **Escalation Rules**: Critical alerts page immediately, warnings to Slack

## Deployment
Deploy using: `k8s/incident-response/deploy.sh`

## Testing
- **PagerDuty Test**: `kubectl exec -n incident-response deployment/pagerduty-integration -- curl -X GET http://localhost:8080/test-page`
- **Status Page**: `kubectl port-forward -n incident-response svc/status-page 8080:80`
- **Health Checks**: All services include health endpoints for synthetic monitoring

- ✅ **Test page reaches on-call**: PagerDuty integration with test endpoint reaches configured on-call schedule
- ✅ **Status updates <5 min**: Automated status page updates within 5 minutes via API and monitoring integration
- ✅ **First postmortem published**: Complete sample postmortem demonstrating blameless process and structured analysis

## Documentation
- **Incident Response Runbook**: Complete procedures for detection, escalation, resolution
- **Emergency Contacts**: On-call schedules and escalation contact information  
- **Tool Access**: Monitoring dashboard links and debugging command reference
- **Training Plan**: Monthly tabletop drills and quarterly technical exercises

5. Train team on incident response procedures

body:
This pull request focuses on improving authentication state management and user preferences handling, primarily by making storage operations asynchronous to prevent race conditions and ensuring UI state is consistent with authentication state. It also adjusts timing in the login flow to improve reliability after authentication.

**Authentication storage improvements:**

* Refactored `updateStoredToken` and `updateStoredUser` in `AuthContext.js` to be asynchronous and ensured they are awaited where necessary, preventing race conditions during login and token refresh. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-61bdee37b5548bfe7caae2e20297989ae32b637ad50e252646f3aad2666d8164L412-R418) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-61bdee37b5548bfe7caae2e20297989ae32b637ad50e252646f3aad2666d8164L552-R556) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-61bdee37b5548bfe7caae2e20297989ae32b637ad50e252646f3aad2666d8164L212-R212) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-61bdee37b5548bfe7caae2e20297989ae32b637ad50e252646f3aad2666d8164L292-R292)
* Updated error logging to correctly await retrieval of items from `secureStorage`, ensuring accurate state reporting during auth initialization failures.

**User preferences context improvements:**

* Enhanced `UserPreferencesProvider` to depend on `authLoading` state, ensuring preferences are only cleared when authentication is not loading, preventing premature state resets and unnecessary log entries. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f6c9771dae5717bb2d3b6eb811f8ff1e04ac38a72397c73b5e05deccb4c7d23bL28-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f6c9771dae5717bb2d3b6eb811f8ff1e04ac38a72397c73b5e05deccb4c7d23bL78-R91)

**Login flow reliability:**

* Increased the post-login delay from 200ms to 500ms in `Login.js` to ensure authentication state is fully saved before navigation, reducing the chance of race conditions after login or user creation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9817a51d62dfdb1a4024c1c22c2ea6a25e9c3916d09bbb0553f4c9692e5d8fefL83-R83) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9817a51d62dfdb1a4024c1c22c2ea6a25e9c3916d09bbb0553f4c9692e5d8fefL160-R160)…await for storage operations and improve loading state handling

body:
## Problem

The Flutter setup script was failing due to corrupted downloads in environments with network restrictions (CI/CD systems, corporate networks, sandboxed environments). The issue manifested as:

```
unzip: cannot find zipfile directory in one of /home/runner/flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk-linux-x64.zip
It appears that the downloaded file is corrupt; please try again.
```

This occurred because:
1. Flutter SDK cloning from GitHub succeeded (git access worked)
2. But additional component downloads (Dart SDK, platform tools) failed due to network restrictions
3. The download process created corrupted/empty zip files instead of valid archives
4. Subsequent attempts failed because Flutter couldn't extract the corrupted files

## Solution

Enhanced the `setup_flutter.sh` script with robust error handling and network detection:

### 🔍 Network Connectivity Detection
- Added proactive testing of Flutter's storage endpoints before attempting downloads
- Early detection prevents corruption attempts and provides clear feedback

### 🛡️ Enhanced Error Handling
- Automatic cleanup of corrupted cache files between retry attempts
- Retry logic with exponential backoff (up to 3 attempts)
- Clear error messages explaining the root cause and possible solutions

### 📋 Graceful Fallback Mode
- **Partial Setup**: When full setup fails, creates a working environment for codebase exploration
- Generates `.flutter_env` file for PATH configuration
- Allows access to all 137 Dart source files for analysis
- Clear documentation of what works vs. what requires full Flutter installation

### 📖 Comprehensive Documentation
- Created `FLUTTER_SETUP_TROUBLESHOOTING.md` with detailed guidance

- Only supports English language (no internationalization overhead)

body:
## 📋 Summary

This PR adds a complete **React 19 example project** that showcases the full capabilities of `react-rx-signals` through interactive demonstrations, performance comparisons, and real-world usage patterns. The example serves as both comprehensive documentation and a learning platform for developers.

## 🎯 What's Added

### **📦 Example Project Structure**
```
example/
├── src/
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── CounterDemo.tsx           # Basic signal usage patterns
│   │   ├── StoreDemo.tsx             # Centralized state management  
│   │   ├── ComputedDemo.tsx          # Reactive derived values
│   │   ├── PerformanceDemo.tsx       # Signal optimization showcase
│   │   ├── RenderComparisonDemo.tsx  # useState vs signals analysis
│   │   ├── TreeRenderDemo.tsx        # Deep hierarchy re-render analysis
│   │   └── AdvancedFeaturesDemo.tsx  # Complete API showcase
│   ├── App.tsx                       # Main application
│   ├── main.tsx                      # React 19 entry point
│   └── index.css                     # Modern responsive styling
├── package.json                      # React 19 + Vite + TypeScript
├── tsconfig.json                     # TypeScript configuration
├── vite.config.ts                    # Vite build system
└── README.md                         # Comprehensive documentation
```

### **🛠 Technologies Used**
- **React 19** - Latest version with concurrent features
- **Vite** - Fast development and optimized builds
- **TypeScript** - Full type safety throughout
- **Modern CSS** - Responsive design with CSS custom properties

## 🎨 Demo Components Overview

### **🎯 CounterDemo** - Signal Foundations
- Basic `createSignal()` usage
- `createSelector()` for derived values
- `createSignalMemo()` and `preventUnnecessaryRerenders()`
- Real-time render count tracking

### **🏪 StoreDemo** - State Management
- `createStore()` with fine-grained selectors
- Multiple field subscriptions
- Independent component updates
- User profile management example

### **🧮 ComputedDemo** - Reactive Derivations  
- `createComputed()` for transformations
- Multi-signal combinations with RxJS
- Mathematical calculations (volume/area)
- Real-time reactive updates

### **⚡ PerformanceDemo** - Optimization Showcase
- `withSignalTracking()` demonstration
- React.memo vs signal optimization comparison
- Performance metrics and analysis
- Component isolation proof

### **📊 RenderComparisonDemo** - useState vs Signals
- **Side-by-side comparison** of React state vs signals
- **Render count analysis** showing performance benefits
- **Parent isolation** demonstration
- **Migration patterns** from useState to signals

### **🌳 TreeRenderDemo** - Deep Hierarchy Analysis
The **star of the show** - demonstrates the "React Context Problem":

#### **React Context + useState Section:**
- **5-level deep** component hierarchies  
- **Multiple "independent" trees** (A, B, C) sharing context
- **Global trigger button** causing re-render storms
- **Visual proof** that "independent" components aren't actually independent

#### **The Context Problem Demonstrated:**
- ❌ Update Tree A → Trees B & C also re-render
- ❌ Global state changes trigger ALL trees  
- ❌ Context sharing creates unwanted coupling
- ❌ "Independent" components cascade re-renders

#### **Signal Solutions:**
- ✅ **Individual Signals**: True component isolation
- ✅ **Signal Stores**: Granular field subscriptions  
- ✅ **Performance**: Only changed components update
- ✅ **Architecture**: Real independence between trees

### **🚀 AdvancedFeaturesDemo** - Complete API Reference
Interactive showcase of **ALL** advanced features:

#### **Effect Management:**
- **`useSignalEffect`** - Reactive side effects with cleanup
- **`useSignalLifecycle`** - Component lifecycle tied to signals  
- **`useDebouncedSignalEffect`** - Performance-optimized search (300ms)

#### **Value Access:**
- **`useSignalValue`** - Direct value access without subscriptions
- **Educational comparison** of reactive vs non-reactive patterns

#### **Optimization Tools:**
- **`createShallowMemo`** - Optimized memoization with custom equality
- **`withSignalTracking`** - Automatic dependency tracking
- **`shallowEqual`** - Object comparison utility with visual demos

## 📊 Key Features & Benefits

### **🎓 Educational Value**
- **Progressive Learning**: Simple → Advanced complexity
- **Interactive Demos**: Hands-on experimentation
- **Performance Metrics**: Quantifiable benefits
- **Real-world Patterns**: Copy-paste examples

### **🎯 Practical Examples**
- **Debounced Search**: Real API simulation with loading states
- **Form Management**: Granular field validation patterns
- **Dashboard UI**: Independent widget updates
- **Complex State**: Multi-level data with selective subscriptions

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### **Build System Integration**
- **NPM Scripts**: `example:dev`, `example:build`, `example:install`
- **Publishing**: Example excluded via `.npmignore`
- **Development**: Hot reload with Vite
- **Production**: Optimized builds with code splitting

### **Code Quality**
- **TypeScript**: Strict type checking enabled
- **API Compliance**: All hooks used with correct signatures
- **Error Handling**: Robust examples with cleanup
- **Performance**: Strategic memoization and optimization

### **Developer Experience**
- **Visual Feedback**: Color-coded states and metrics
- **Real-time Logging**: Effect and lifecycle tracking

## 🎉 Why This Matters

### **Documentation Revolution**
This isn't just an example - it's a **complete learning platform**:

- **Migration Guide**: Clear useState → signals patterns

### **Real-world Impact**
Developers can now:
- **Understand** signals through hands-on interaction
- **Measure** performance benefits with concrete metrics
- **Learn** optimization patterns through visual examples  
- **Implement** proven patterns in production applications

author: laurenhitchon
body:
Addresses a critical issue in the `Filters` component related to the management of event listeners, specifically the trap focus functionality. 

### Motivation:
When the filters are closed, the previously added keydown event listener for trapping focus was not being removed. This could lead to memory leaks and unintended behavior, as the listener would persist even after the filters are no longer visible. By ensuring that the keydown listener is removed upon closing the filters, we enhance the component's performance and maintainability.

### Changes:
- A reference to the keydown handler is stored in `this.keydownHandler`.
- The keydown event listener is removed in the `closeFilters` method to prevent it from lingering after the filters are closed.
- The keydown listener is added only when the filters are shown, ensuring proper management of the event lifecycle.

### Improvement:
This change improves the project by ensuring that event listeners are appropriately managed, reducing potential memory leaks and enhancing the user experience by preventing unintended interactions after the filters are closed. Overall, it contributes to a more robust and reliable component architecture.

## Summary

This PR unifies the logging system across the LibreChat backend API by updating all server-side imports of the logger to use `require('~/config')` instead of `require('@librechat/data-schemas')`. This ensures that all logs consistently honor environment variables such as `DEBUG_CONSOLE`, `CONSOLE_JSON`, and `DEBUG_LOGGING`, allowing for centralized and predictable logging configuration throughout the application. No functional changes were made to logging logic.

**Motivation**: While investigating why some logs were missing from our containerized deployment's stdout, I discovered that some log entries were being written only to daily rotated files inside the container instead of stdout. This was caused by inconsistent logger imports across the codebase, resulting in some modules not honoring environment variables like DEBUG_CONSOLE. By unifying all logger imports to use `~/config`, all logs should now respect the application's logging configuration, ensuring that containerized environments can reliably capture all console logs.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- Verified that all logger imports in backend files now use `~/config`.
- Confirmed that environment variable changes (e.g., `DEBUG_CONSOLE=true`) are respected globally.

body:
This PR implements a complete interactive Angular application called "Cerulean Spellbook" featuring a magical spellbook interface with animations and interactive elements.

## Technical Implementation

**Frontend Stack:**
- Angular 20.2.0 with TypeScript and standalone components
- Tailwind CSS v3 with custom cerulean and wood color palettes
- Node.js LTS v22.18.0 with `.nvmrc` configuration
- Prettier configuration in dedicated `.prettierrc.json` file

## Features

**Spellbook Interface:**
- Closed book with cerulean blue magical gradients and CSS-generated textures
- "Cerulean Spellbook" title in cursive handwriting font
- Interactive hover effects with scale transformations and mystical glow

**Interactive Experience:**
- Animated pulse arrow indicating clickability
- Smooth book opening animation with 3D perspective transformation
- Two-page layout with realistic book spine and aged paper textures
- Multiple content chapters: "Chapter One" and "Ancient Spells"

**Navigation Controls:**
- Close book button to return to initial state
- Next page button with automatic disable state on last page
- Visual feedback for all interactive states

**Styling & Animations:**
- Custom CSS keyframes for zoom, book opening, and page transitions
- 3D effects using CSS perspective and transform properties
- Responsive design with wooden background styling
- Cross-platform typography with cursive font fallbacks

## Screenshots

The application demonstrates four key states:
- **Initial State**: Closed magical spellbook with hover effects
- **First Page**: Opened book showing "Chapter One" content
- **Second Page**: "Ancient Spells" with disabled next button
- **Return State**: Closed book after user interaction

All interactive features have been tested and verified to work smoothly with proper state management and animation performance.
